deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics: no formulas, computations or derivations. It is a passage of Riemann's speculative natural philosophy (Naturphilosophie), continuing the 'Erdseele' (earth-soul) argument of the previous page. The argument runs as follows.

(Premise from the previous page.) The 'Geistesmassen' (mind-masses) produced by organisms persist after death. To explain the planned development of organic nature, they must enter a larger interwoven mind-mass, the earth-soul. Any combination of mind-masses, at least of different kinds, requires a material physical process. Only ponderable (weighable) matter can be the substrate of mental activity.

(a) It is a fact that the solid crust and everything ponderable above it does not serve one common mental process. Its motions are explained by other causes.

(b) Directly beneath the solidified crust, all conditions known to be necessary for a 'Denkprocess' (thinking process) appear to be met.

(1) Supporting reason. For the relative motions of matter to be determined by internal processes, external moving causes (sunlight, solar heat) must affect the relative position of the parts as little as possible. In organisms this shielding grows with the height of the mental functions served. In the earth's interior it must hold to a higher degree than any organic arrangement on the surface could achieve.

(2) Main objection. On the whole surface only the four 'organic elements' (C, H, O, N) carry organic life.

(Reply, numbered '1,'.) It is absurd to suppose that the organic arose from the inorganic on the solid crust. Explaining even the lowest organisms already presupposes an 'organising principle'.

(Conclusion, after a horizontal rule.) Only one assumption remains: the ponderable masses inside the solid crust carry the earth's soul-life.

(Programme.) Are these masses suited to that role? What are the external conditions for a life-process? The general experience of observable life-processes must be the basis. Only insofar as we can explain them may we draw conclusions that also apply to other domains of phenomena. The next page lists these conditions: shielding, physical processes, porous non-crystalline matter, the four elements, temperature limits.

A later pencil note in the margin, probably by an editor, reads '(Von hier an bis S. 32 wohl wegzulassen) ??' (from here up to p. 32 probably to be omitted). This marks the passage as a candidate for omission from the edition.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors.

Scientifically, the reply to objection (2) rests on the vitalist rejection of abiogenesis ('ungereimt'). Wöhler's 1828 urea synthesis had already undercut the strict organic/inorganic divide. The claim that the earth's interior shields matter better than organisms do is speculative and was never quantified.

The objection marked '2,' is answered by an item numbered '1,'. This is a numbering inconsistency, or the start of an unfinished sub-list of replies. The objection about the four organic elements is not actually answered for the earth's interior.

results.what: Hypothesis that ponderable matter beneath the solid crust carries an 'earth-soul' (Erdseele). It is supported by the claim that it is maximally shielded from external disturbances such as solar light and heat.
results.usually_credited_to: G. T. Fechner (Zend-Avesta, 1851; Nanna, 1848); Riemann's interest in Fechner is well documented

results.what: Principle that higher life-processes require greater shielding of the carrier from external moving causes.
results.modern_name: Vitalist/physiological heuristic (cf. homeostasis, Bernard's milieu intérieur)
results.usually_credited_to: Claude Bernard (milieu intérieur, 1850s–1870s) for the related physiological idea

results.what: Rejection of abiogenesis on the earth's surface and postulate of an 'organising principle'.

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann's Fechner-influenced naturphilosophical fragments on Geistesmassen and the Erdseele are known; parts appear in the Werke ('Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts'). This page adds a non-mathematical detail: the earth's interior as the seat of the earth-soul. The editorial note suggests it was deliberately omitted from print. It is of mild biographical/philosophical interest only.
transcription_corrections: Final line: the word after the gap '( ———' appears to read 'sind.' ("...welche auch auf andere Erscheinungskreise anwendbar sind."), not 'Theil[?]'.
Line 'in desto höherem Grade statt, zu höheren (geistigen) Processen' probably reads 'zu je höheren (geistigen) Processen sie dienen' (the 'je' is faint).
The pencil header 'Riemann 18' and the margin note '(Von hier an bis S. 32 wohl wegzulassen) ??' are in a later hand, probably archival or editorial, not Riemann's.
'äußerer Beobachtung' is likely Riemann's own form (= 'der äußeren Beobachtung'); keep it as written.
